kept.title: The map (02 §1) and the root theorem (01 §4), the two results the fronts lead with, get no prior-art verdict; the map's regions are branching-time path formulas and the core is the greatest bisimulation
kept.evidence: 08:480 "None of the central results is new mathematics: each is near-definitional or a known result restated"; its table (484-496) has no row for «根» or for generation-and-degeneration. 02:17 "延 ... (coinductive); 尽 ... (inductive)". ONE-PAGE:11 "a course can *generate* ... *keep* ... or *degenerate*". Record 80 (not the chapter): "the core the greatest bisimulation inside the class".
kept.what_is_there: The map's definitions and exclusions are proved for every relation and pair of classes, with calibrations (LPO, WLPO, excluded middle). The root theorem is called "*The root theorem*". Bisimulation (Park 1981; Milner 1989) is named only in the root record and, for constancy, at 01:104. The map's record has no correspondence or prior-art section at all.
kept.what_is_missing: A verdict for both results. 延 is the greatest fixed point "some path goes on" (CTL EG / νX.◇X; Aubin's viability kernel). 尽 is the least fixed point "every path ends" (AF of a dead end; the well-founded part). 生成 is a fair-path formula (E GF renewal), and 后守 is E FG ¬renewal. The calibrations are the known Σ/Π-level cost of deciding "eventually always" against "infinitely often" in constructive reverse mathematics. The core is the greatest bisimulation inside a class, which exists by Knaster–Tarski. None of these is cited in 01 §4, 02 §1, 08 §8 or the fronts. Checked with grep: there is no 'branching-time', 'CTL', 'mu-calculus', 'Büchi' or 'well-founded' in the chapters, and 'Park' / 'Milner' / 'Knaster' do not appear in 01, 02 or 08.
kept.why_it_matters: A reader of ONE-PAGE and THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING is shown the map and the core as the root's results. 08 says none of the central results is new, but the two most visible ones are left out of the table that says so, so a reader is likely to take them as new. Placed against branching-time logic, the map's exclusions are near-definitional, and the two-grain reading (传) is the part to defend.
kept.suggested_work: Add a row to 08 §8 for the root theorem (greatest bisimulation; Park 1981, Knaster–Tarski: near-definitional) and one for the map. The map row should give its regions as path formulas (EG, AF, fair EG / E GF, E FG), point to the viability kernel and the well-founded part, and give a verdict (likely near-definitional, with 传 at two grains as the delta). Name bisimulation beside «根» in 01 §4 and in the generation record's correspondence section. Then ask the audit's third-part question of the two-grain law (`«阶生成则上不退化»`).
kept.verify_reason: Half of this is already done. 01-ROOT.md:104 says that for a class constancy "is bisimulation equivalence". The record continuation-relative-to-a-class.md:80 cites Park 1981 and Milner 1989 and calls the core "the greatest bisimulation inside the class". degeneration-from-a-horizon.md:64 reads 尽 as well-foundedness. So the claim that the core's prior art appears nowhere in the chapters is wrong. What does hold: the 08 §8 table (08-METHOD.md:484-496) and the fronts (ONE-PAGE:11, THE-THEORY:67/75) give no verdict row for «根» or for generation-and-degeneration. The generation record's prior-art paragraph (line 73) names only autopoiesis, Montévil–Mossio and Rosas. None of 02 §1, its records or 08 links 延/尽/生成/后守 to greatest and least fixed points or CTL path formulas (EG, AF, EGF, EFG). The LPO/WLPO calibrations are not tied to the known arithmetical-hierarchy cost of persistence against recurrence. The blanket verdict at 08:480 already tells a reader none of this is new, so this is a gap in the picture, not a misleading claim.
kept.corrected: 08 §8 gives no verdict row for the root theorem or for the map's regions, the two results the fronts lead with. kept.title: Closed capture (02 §9, T7) and the self-confirming reading loop (03 §12) are one structure, unlinked; the remedy the cited frameworks give (experimentation, persistent excitation) is not brought in
kept.evidence: 02:428 "a reading of the loss is one sufficient way out, not shown the only one". 03:532 "A formation's model is revised only by what its own course exposes, and that course is chosen through the model ... related to self-confirming equilibrium (Fudenberg and Levine 1993) ... none of those works' theorems is reproduced ... What tells such worlds apart comes from beyond the formation's own selection: an act that risks the task, or a reading from outside". 08:505 "Capture through the rule is observability with the reader inside the plant ... and closed-loop identifiability (... Borkar and Varaiya 1979)".
kept.what_is_there: 02 §9 proves that a loop whose rule and reading are formed from the share is invariant under what it does not read (`ClosedCapture.courses_alike_iff_unread`, `lock_outlives_loss`). 03 §12 proves that a model chosen through its own course is never refuted off that course (`ReadingLoop.alike_within`). Closed-loop identifiability is cited, but only in 08.
kept.what_is_missing: No link either way: grep finds 0 references from 02 or the capture records to 03's reading loop, and none back. The stronger results of the cited frameworks are not contained. Closed-loop identification is restored by persistent excitation, and dual control trades probing against performance (Borkar–Varaiya 1979; Feldbaum 1960). Self-confirming equilibria become Nash equilibria under enough experimentation (Fudenberg and Kreps 1993; Fudenberg and Levine 1993). The account's own analogues of that remedy are not connected to these results or to each other: 03's "an act that risks the task", 02's reading of the loss in time (`ReadInTime`), and 明 as coupling reaching beyond the share.
kept.why_it_matters: This is the Zhuang/Hadfield-Menell pattern for a second framework. T7's open question, whether a reading of the loss is the only way out, has a known answer in adaptive control and learning in games: exploration or excitation is another way out. Bringing it in would give T7 a refuter that can be met (a lock left by excitation with no reading of the loss). As it stands, the account's main failure mode for alignment, a measure kept by what it selects, sits in two chapters under two names.
kept.suggested_work: State in 02 §9 and 03 §12 that closed capture is the share-level case of the course chosen through its model, ideally with one Lean bridge: `Unread` gives `alike_within` on the two-level step. Add a law, or a stated correspondence, for the excitation remedy: an act or reading that separates the share's classes at some reading steps unlocks the course, the analogue of persistent excitation. Name Fudenberg–Kreps and Borkar–Varaiya there, and add the resulting forbidden case to T7.
kept.verify_reason: The split is real. 02 §9 (lines 386-447) has no link to 03 §12 or to its records. 03 §12 (520-558) and the records what-a-course-chosen-through-its-model-does-not-test and closed-capture do not refer to each other. 03:384 links 'Learning within capture' to 02's closed capture, but from §8, not from the reading loop. The remedy part is overstated. 03:532 already names the account's analogue of experimentation ("an act that risks the task, or a reading from outside") and cites safe-exploration results (Sui et al. 2015; Turchetta et al. 2016). What is missing: Fudenberg–Kreps/Levine (self-confirming equilibria become Nash under enough experimentation) and persistent excitation or dual control are not brought in. T7's list of ways out (02:428) does not name the act that risks the task, and 03's remedy is not tied to 02's ReadInTime or to 明.
kept.already_at: theories/becoming/chapters/03-KNOWING.md:532 (experimentation and safe exploration); theories/becoming/chapters/03-KNOWING.md:384 (link from §8 to closed capture)
kept.corrected: 02 §9's capture loop and 03 §12's model-confirmed-along-its-own-course are the same shape: the unread is never exposed by a selection through what it reads. Neither links the other. 03 §12 names experimentation as a way out (an act risking the task, safe exploration); 02's T7 lists only readings and does not name it. The stronger results on experimentation (Fudenberg–Kreps 1993; persistent excitation in closed-loop identification, Borkar–Varaiya 1979, already cited at 08:505) are not stated against either.

kept.title: The converse of rest, listed as not shown, is the completeness of ranking functions and the converse Lyapunov theorem; rest (02 §4) and return or attraction (02 §2) are never joined as LaSalle and Conley join them
kept.evidence: 01:165 "The ending is sufficient, not what rest is, and no converse is established. Rest is not being drawn, either way"; 01:170 "Not shown: ... a converse of the law of rest"; 08:487 "ranking functions (Floyd 1967); Lyapunov; LaSalle; chip-firing | restated"; 02:65 "The main law is near-definitional, not a classical attractor".
kept.what_is_there: Rest by a non-rising amount with a least loss (`Amounts.rests`, `«尽则不屡»`). Drawn exactly where not returning (`Law.drawn_iff_not_returns`). Within listed configurations every course enters what returns, and each basin holds one cycle (`Law.enters_returning_within`, `Law.basin_one_cycle`). LaSalle is named in the record and in 08 only.
kept.what_is_missing: The classical joins. (a) Ranking functions are complete for termination, and converse Lyapunov theorems hold (Turing 1949; Floyd 1967; Massera 1949): where marked steps do not recur, an amount that falls exactly at them exists. That is the converse 01 lists as open. (b) LaSalle's invariance principle: a run under a non-rising amount ends in the largest invariant set on which nothing falls. (c) Conley's decomposition: configurations split into recurrent ones and gradient-like ones with a complete Lyapunov function. In finite form that is §2's returning/drawn split joined to §4's ranking: a function strictly falling on every drawn configuration and constant on cycles. grep finds no 'Massera', 'Conley', 'chain recurrent' or 'well-founded' in the chapters.
kept.why_it_matters: 01 presents rest and being drawn as two notions with no converse. A reader takes that as an open gap in the root when a standard theorem closes it. Joining them would make 'what ends' (§4) and 'where a course goes' (§2) one law, as the chapter's thesis suggests.
kept.suggested_work: Prove in the core, on listed configurations with a determined law: (i) the steps-to-cycle count is a ranking that falls at every drawn step and is zero on returning configurations, the finite Conley/LaSalle law; (ii) the converse of `«尽则不屡»` where marked steps are decided. Calibrate the constructive cost of (ii). Then cite LaSalle, Massera and Conley in 02 §4 and update 01 §7's 'Not shown'.
kept.verify_reason: Rest and drawing are explicitly related at 01-ROOT.md:165: "Rest is not being drawn, either way: a fixed point is at rest and not drawn (`«止而不入之例»`), and a place can be drawn in while its marked steps recur (`«入而屡之例»`)". So "never joined" is wrong. The constructive status of the converse is addressed in rest-exactly-where-falls-stop.md (Does not show: classically, with dependent choice, the conditions coincide; line 59 on well-foundedness). The discrete LaSalle principle is cited in rest-theorem-in-any-amounts.md:57, and Floyd, Lyapunov and LaSalle in 08:487. What remains is small. Conley's decomposition is not cited. The classical completeness of ranking functions (Turing, Floyd; converse Lyapunov, Massera) is not named as the converse 01:170 lists as open. That converse is classical and choice-dependent, which the core cannot assert anyway.
kept.corrected: 01:170 lists a converse of the law of rest as not shown. It does not say that classically, with dependent choice, this converse is the known completeness of ranking functions and converse Lyapunov theorems. Only rest-exactly-where-falls-stop.md notes the constructive gap. Conley's recurrent/gradient decomposition, the finite analogue of joining §2's returning/drawn split to §4's ranking, is not cited. The rest/drawn relation itself is already stated at 01:165.

kept.title: Feedback is four separate notions: 01 §1's 'line returning to a class', 02 §7's unsigned coupling loops, 02 §8's regulation with no loop, 02 §9's selection loop; the join 01 claims is not shown
kept.evidence: 01:35 "a feedback loop is a line returning to a class ... The loops of the map ... are of this kind"; 02:313 "A *loop* is a chain of couplings back to its start"; 02:343 "A self-loop of strength `M` has factor `1 + M`"; 02:388 "the loop holds itself"; 03:130 "Open. An instance of the rooms on the World's flows, by which the laws of regulation would apply to them formally"; 08:493 "Maruyama (1963)".
kept.what_is_there: Coupling loops with natural-number strengths, which only amplify (`carried_le_geomBound`, `LoopReturn.nothing_between`). Two-sided regulation and late reading (`Flow.withinGap_iff_between`, `Regulation.no_narrower_band`), stated with no loop. Capture loops on two-level courses. 03's thermostat rooms, explicitly not instances of 02 §8.
kept.what_is_missing: No Lean module defining `onLoop` mentions the grammar, so 01's claim that §7's loops are lines returning to a class is prose only. Strengths carry no sign, so a negative (regulating) loop cannot be a §7 loop. §8 never mentions loops, and §9's loop is never related to §7's. Maruyama's (1963) deviation-amplifying versus deviation-counteracting loops, decided by the sign of the loop product, and the small-gain theorem (Zames 1966) are what join these. Maruyama is cited only in 08, and there is no 'small-gain' or 'Zames' in the repository.
kept.why_it_matters: Runaway, regulation and capture are three of the map's main mechanisms, and 01 tells the reader they are one kind. They are not shown to be. A signed loop law would also forbid something testable: settling with no counteracting loop upstream.
kept.suggested_work: Give §7's strengths a sign, or a paired opposing strength, and prove that a difference settles within a band only through a loop whose net return is below one: the discrete small-gain law. State §8's two-sided regulation as such a loop, and §9's `ReadsShare` as a positive loop of the two-level step. Add a lemma tying `onLoop` to a line under a class, or withdraw 01:35's 'of this kind'. Close 03:130 by instancing the rooms on §8.
kept.verify_reason: Overstated. 02 §7 does treat counteracting loops. 'Whether a loop closes a difference' (02:343ff) says "a loop closes a difference only through a link giving back less; a map below the identity off zero closes within d turns". So "a negative (regulating) loop cannot be a §7 loop" is wrong. 01:35's join is an explicit modelling reading (dated occurrences), not a claimed theorem. The capture record a-reading-against-the-share-does-not-ratchet.md:45 reads one capture law as "Negative feedback from those a selection disfavours". Two things are real. 02 §8's regulation (an opposing exchange settling at m) is never called a loop and never related to §7's closing loop. 01:35 illustrates feedback with a thermostat, a regulating case, yet points to §7's runaway loops (r-how-a-carried-difference-grows) and not to §8. Maruyama's amplifying/counteracting distinction is cited only in 08:493.
kept.corrected: 02 §8's regulation is a counteracting feedback loop, but it is never related to 02 §7's loops, including §7's own law that a loop with a link giving back less closes a difference. 01:35 illustrates feedback with a thermostat (regulation) but links only to §7's runaway loops. The amplifying/counteracting split (Maruyama 1963) that would join them is cited only in 08's table.

kept.title: 02's going-on-along-some-branch, its keeping-s sub-process, its point of no return, 03's largest closed region and 05's Viability kernels are one notion (viability and invariance kernels, Aubin), never joined
kept.evidence: 02:17 "延 ... `x` lies in a family each member of which is continued within it (coinductive)"; 02:81 "Keeping only the steps after which `s` can still be had keeps `s`, holds every sub-process keeping `s`"; 03:555 "the largest region inside it closed under the relation (`«所闭之承最大»`); at a process's steps it is the invariance kernel (`Viability.kernel_iff_held`)"; record:64 "it is also Aubin's viability kernel".
kept.what_is_there: Each piece is proved in its own module. 延 is a coinductive greatest family. The juncture law gives the largest sub-process keeping `s`. `RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below` gives an exact point of no return. 03 and 05 have `Viability.kernel`, plans and certificates (`never_leaves_iff_certificate`).
kept.what_is_missing: 02 never mentions a viability or invariance kernel. 03 and 05 never link back to 02 §1's 延 or 02 §2's junctures; grep finds no 'juncture' in 03, 05 or 07. Viability theory (Aubin 1991) relates these pieces. 延 is the viability kernel of 'the pattern goes on'. The juncture is the boundary of the kernel of 'reach `s`', and the regulation map is the keeping sub-process. The point of no return is the boundary of the kernel of 'level at or above need'. Aubin is cited only in 03 and 05 records.
kept.why_it_matters: 02 §2's attraction and juncture laws are handed to no later chapter. 02:7 hands §§3–5 and §7 onward, not §2. So the root's account of how something keeps a possibility is disconnected from the guards, plans and judgment in 03, 05 and 07 that use the same fixed point.
kept.suggested_work: Prove in the grammar: 延 is the viability kernel (greatest family closed under 'has a successor in it') and `«所闭之承最大»` is the invariance kernel, related as ∃ and ∀ duals, equal under a fixed successor (record 64 already states this for Viability). Restate `Branching.no_juncture_of_keeps` as 'the juncture is the kernel's boundary', and the regime's point of no return as the kernel boundary for its guard. Link 02 §§1, 2 and 5 to 03:555 and 05 §8 both ways.
kept.verify_reason: "One notion" is wrong. The repository deliberately separates the invariance kernel (every course stays) from the viability kernel (some course stays). a-response-common-over-a-reading.md:64 says they coincide only where each configuration has one successor. market-protected-continuation.md:108 records a correction from 'viability' to 'invariance' kernel. The invariance-kernel side is already joined: 03:555 and Viability.lean prove `Viability.kernel_iff_held` from the grammar's «所闭之承最大» (01 §7's shared closure law), and 05:107/349 use it. What is real: the existential side in 02 is never named as the viability kernel or related as the dual of the invariance kernel. That side is 02 §1's 延 (a family each member continued within it) and 02 §2's sub-process keeping `s` (02:81). The juncture and the point of no return are not placed relative to either kernel.
kept.corrected: The invariance kernel is joined to the grammar (03:555, Viability.lean, 05). Its existential dual is not: 02 §1's 延 and 02 §2's largest sub-process keeping `s` are viability kernels, never named so and never related to the invariance kernel or to the juncture and point of no return as kernel boundaries.

kept.title: Stochastic stability (Kandori–Mailath–Rob, Young) and Arthur's urn are cited beside the capture laws, but their stronger results (long-run selection independent of the start, exit by noise) are not brought in, and T7's 'locked for good' holds only without noise
kept.evidence: 02:394 "so only a change of the law, of how the rule reads or of the selection leaves"; 02:438 "without noise the start decides, while under rare mutation the long-run state is the risk-dominant one (Kandori, Mailath and Rob 1993; Young 1993)"; COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION:55 "cited, not proved"; record:60 "the lock-in of increasing returns (Arthur 1989), here decided by the start rather than by random arrivals".
kept.what_is_there: Noise-free count models in which every course read from the share is locked one way (`DrawnShaping.drawn_locked_either`), with a window and a deadline for a reading in time. Noise is listed as open (02:467).
kept.what_is_missing: Two results are not contained. Under persistent small noise the lock is left with no reading of the loss, after a waiting time exponential in population size and in the risk-dominance gap; the long-run state is the risk-dominant one wherever 2c < hi + lo. Under increasing returns (Arthur's Pólya-type urn) lock-in holds almost surely. These two sort the §9 models into those whose lock survives noise (counts that accumulate, as in `ChoiceCountCapture`) and those whose lock does not (constant `hi`, `lo`, `c`, as in `DrawnShaping`). The sorting is not stated.
kept.why_it_matters: T7 and 07 §6's second condition (a lock left in time) rest on locks being permanent. A reader is told what ends a lock; under the cited result, noise ends it as well, and which side wins in the long run does not depend on the start. This is also a ready refuter design: exit frequency against the predicted exponent.
kept.suggested_work: In the periphery, prove the two-kind stag-hunt case with mutation rate ε: the risk-dominant lock is stochastically stable, with exit time of order ε^(−N·gap). Prove the urn case separately. Then add to 02 §9 and T7 which §9 models' locks survive noise, and a forbidden case on noise-driven exit.
kept.verify_reason: Mostly already integrated. The long-run result of stochastic stability is stated with its condition at 02-MAP.md:438: "under rare mutation the long-run state is the risk-dominant one (Kandori, Mailath and Rob 1993; Young 1993), the shapers' wherever `2c < hi + lo`". COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md:55 draws its consequence: "Over long horizons the window may then be transient, and an exit would need a change of `hi`, `lo` or `c`, not timing alone." 02:414 states "the courses are without noise", and the shaping record line 34 says the critical mass bounds courses without noise only. Not brought in: the exponential waiting time of noise-driven exit; Arthur's almost-sure lock-in for counted choices (`ChoiceCountCapture`); a sorting of the §9 models by whether their lock survives noise. T7's own statement (02:428) also carries no noise caveat.
kept.corrected: The long-run risk-dominant result and its consequence for the window are already stated (02:438; COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION:55). Still missing: T7's thesis text does not say its 'for good' holds only without noise; the §9 models are not sorted into those whose lock survives noise (accumulating counts, Arthur's urn) and those whose lock it can leave (constant hi, lo, c); the exit time under noise is not given.

kept.title: Capture's 'lock', 'meta-attractor' and 'point of no return' borrow §2's attraction and §5's threshold law by name only; one perturbation law is proved twice under two names
kept.evidence: 02:76 "a perturbed state is drawn back at once (`Law.perturbation_drawnInto`)" against 02:391 "a perturbed state is re-absorbed in one step (`Law.perturbation_reabsorbed`)". Both take the same hypothesis `byRule : ∀ x x' g, next (x, g) = next (x', g)` (Branching.lean, SeekingRuns.lean). 02:402 "元吸引子 (meta-attractor)"; 02:262 "*One law of exact thresholds.* ... Every threshold below is its case"; 02:440 "the point of no return belongs to the share's course".
kept.what_is_there: §2 proves that drawn into an absorbing region is exactly not returning. §9 proves that locked courses have shares rising strictly. §5 has a general exact-threshold law, `RegimeMargin.leading_exact`, which is used only inside RegimeMargin.lean.
kept.what_is_missing: Three statements are missing. A locked course whose share rises strictly does not return, so it is drawn by `Law.drawn_iff_not_returns` (the meta-attractor as an attractor in §2's sense). The critical mass (`DrawnShaping.critical_iff`) and the read-in-time window are cases of the one threshold law. The two perturbation theorems should be merged or one derived from the other.
kept.why_it_matters: The chapter names its capture loop an attractor and its window a point of no return, while §2 says its attraction 'is not a classical attractor' and §5's threshold law reaches only the regime. The words claim a unity the laws do not show.
kept.suggested_work: Add a corollary in RuleCapture/DrawnShaping: a strictly favoured start is drawn into the locked region (from `drawn_rises` with `Law.drawn_iff_not_returns`). Prove the critical mass from `leading_exact`, or generalize that law to any down-closed fate on a linearly ordered state. Retire one perturbation name.
kept.verify_reason: The two perturbation theorems share the hypothesis `byRule` but prove different conclusions. `Law.perturbation_drawnInto` (Branching.lean:1181) concludes `DrawnInto next (· = next (x, g)) (x', g)`. `Law.perturbation_reabsorbed` (SeekingRuns.lean:49) concludes orbit equality from step 1, as an instance of `Law.reabsorbed`. So they are not one law proved twice, though neither text relates them. 02:262's "Every threshold below is its case" refers to the §5 regime table that follows, not to §9's critical mass, so no unity is falsely claimed there. That the meta-attractor (02:402) is drawn in §2's sense (`Law.drawn_iff_not_returns`) is not stated: true but minor.
kept.corrected: Two closely related perturbation laws, one drawn-into (02:76) and one orbit-coincidence (02:391), take the same hypothesis and are not related in text. The meta-attractor is not stated to be attracting in §2's sense. The critical mass and the read-in-time window are not placed under §5's threshold law, which does not claim them.

kept.title: Place/transition nets are mapped on balance and dissipation only; net theory's own dynamics (liveness, T-invariants, Commoner's siphon–trap theorem), which match 02's generation, return and rest, are not brought in

kept.title: Blackwell's comparison is split across §1, §8 and §12 and never stated as one equivalence; 08 credits it to §1, which does not mention it

kept.why_it_matters: Blackwell's theorem is the standard unification of 'what an experiment tells apart' with 'what it is worth for deciding'. kept.title: Posterior consistency and misspecified learning (Doob 1949; Berk 1966; Esponda and Pouzo 2016) are absent, though 03 asserts that seeking corrects within what experiments separate

kept.title: C, the ethics' order, is the impact-measure and option-keeping family, but that is never said where C is defined

Empowerment (Klyubin, Polani and Nehaniv 2005) is not in the account at all. In 07 §6 impact measures are filed as a selection approach.
kept.what_is_missing: Where C is stated (07 §4.4) and in 'what a course keeps reachable' (07 §2) there is no statement that widening and covering are, formally, the reachable-set preservation that impact measures penalize and that power-seeking theorems show optimal agents pursue. Nor are the field's known failure modes carried over to C: interference and offsetting incentives (Krakovna 2019), POWER's tendency to disempower others (Turner 2021), and empowerment-maximization. 07 §6's filing of impact measures as an outside method hides that C belongs to the same family.
kept.why_it_matters: A reader is told that C is the order for life and for AI direction and that it shares only Pareto and Sen's intersection. In alignment, the same object is a known remedy with known pathologies, and an empirical test (SE1) already found the account's measure equal to it. This changes what a reader believes about C's novelty, and about whether C adopted as an objective leads to power-seeking. Nothing in 07 §4 says it does not.
kept.suggested_work: Add a 08 §8 row for C and covering against relative reachability, AUP and POWER, with a verdict. In 07 §4.4 or §6, state the map: covering is reachability-set inclusion, own widening is POWER read as admission, and the inaction baseline is the withheld levels. Then ask for a third part: does C (all formations' admissions, not the agent's own) forbid the power-seeking that POWER's theorems give, under the margin law (`Flow.Balances.widens_iff_others_within`)? State the interference and offsetting incentives as cases or non-cases of C.

The own-widening record (line 62) says 'own widening is option-keeping read as admission'. widening-along-a-reading.md:54 compares against relative reachability. ONE-ARGUMENT:75 / SE1 found the blind draw to be relative reachability on a replayed course. The third-parts AUDIT (ue0-third-parts/AUDIT.md:106, :366) states what is forbidden against Turner and Turner-Stavrianos, and BECOMING-SIGNIFICANCE-REVIEW.md:209-247 gives the formal table (POWER, RR, AUP). Nor are the family's known failure modes, offsetting and interference (Krakovna 2019), brought to C: neither 'offsetting' nor 'interference incentive' appears in the live account. 08 §8 has no row for own widening.
kept.corrected: The tie between C/widening and option-keeping (POWER, relative reachability, AUP) is made in 07 §6 (line 651), the own-widening record, SE1, the significance review and the third-parts audit. It is not made where C and covering are defined (07 §4, 07 §2), nor in 08 §8's known-results rows, which give no RR/AUP/POWER neighbour for covering and have no row for own widening. The chapters use 'invariance kernel' and a `Viability` namespace but cite neither field. 'Holling', 'resilience' and 'panarchy' do not occur in any chapter or front.

There is no 08 §8 row for resilience or viability, and no third-part question against them.

The account's possible addition, the joint draw certified by persistence under a gate, can only be judged against that field.

Add a 08 §8 row: margin and point of no return against Holling, Walker et al. 2004, Aubin 1991 and Martin 2004. kept.corrected: Viability theory's invariance kernel is used and proved on the account's own Viability module in 03 §12 and 05 §11, with Aubin cited only in a record. kept.title: The fourth unification names 'externality' as unified, but no externality economics is in the account
kept.evidence: 08:585 "overshoot, externality and Goodhart's law as one law of the optimum under room"; 05:223 forbids "a side-effect term ranked after the reward protecting a condition"; 'Coase' and 'mechanism design' occur nowhere in the account; 'Pigou' only as Pigou–Dalton
kept.what_is_there: The optimum law and T3 claim one law across overshoot, externality and Goodhart. The audit treats the claim through Zhuang and Hadfield-Menell only.
kept.what_is_missing: No source for externality is cited: Pigou (1920), Coase (1960), Meade (1952), or the mechanism-design line (Hurwicz 1973; Myerson). Their remedies are not mapped onto the account's own: a Pigouvian price is a coupling of the unread loss into the reward, traded off and not ranked after it. Coase bargaining is pooling by exchange of rights, and exclusive footprints are property rights. So it is not shown whether T3's forbidden 'side-effect term ranked after the reward' leaves the classic traded-off Pigouvian remedy standing, or what the account forbids that welfare economics leaves open.
kept.why_it_matters: A reader is told that externality is a case of one law. The field where externality is defined has a theorem: internalization restores efficiency under stated premises. That theorem is the remedy side the account's exits reach for, and it is absent, so the unification is asserted from one side only. This is distinct from the Zhuang case: the frameworks and remedies are economic, not the proxy-update remedy.
kept.suggested_work: Either narrow 08 §9's wording to what is shown, or contain the field. State the Pigouvian case as a law on the optimum: an order rising with the family plus a priced term for the beyond. Find the price at which every optimum keeps the dependence, beside `Optimum.frontier_keeps_stepwise`. State the Coasean case as pooling under transferable rights. Add an 08 §8 row, and ask what third part room gives (for example, a price below the room threshold drains all the same).
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed that the live account cites no Pigou (only Pigou–Dalton), Coase, Meade or mechanism design. The only 'externalit' hits are 05:424 and the 08:585 row. But the Pigouvian remedy is contained in substance: coupling the unread loss into the reward is traded off and stated with exact thresholds. These are the exact-penalty principle (Zangwill 1967) and a step coupling of at least r − q (`Optimum.frontier_keeps_stepwise`; the record a-step-coupling-keeps-at-every-horizon cites per-step impact penalties). So the reader's question is answered: T3's forbidden lexicographic 'side-effect term ranked after the reward' is distinct from a traded-off coupling, which the account supports. The third-parts audit (AUDIT.md:364, 'Pigou's static tax'; 'Known neighbour: Pigouvian taxes in the dynamic commons') already names the welfare-economics contrast. What remains is that the fronts and 08 say 'externality' without its field and without saying that the coupling laws are its Pigouvian remedy.
kept.corrected: 08 §8's fourth unification calls externality unified but cites no externality economics. The account's coupling laws (exact penalty, step coupling) are the Pigouvian remedy in substance, and the audit names Pigou as the contrast, but neither 08 nor 05 says so. Coase, property rights read as exclusive footprints, and mechanism design are not mapped.

kept.title: Coordination needs common knowledge, but the account offers only distributed knowledge, unnamed, while its aim and OPENING turn on coordination
kept.evidence: OPENING:39 "The wisdom exists, but we cannot coordinate."; 05:244 pooled coupling "as with distributed knowledge" (no citation); RF PLAN:268 "Aumann's theorem ... is a candidate grammar statement, recorded as a debt"; 'common knowledge' occurs in no chapter or front
kept.what_is_there: Pools (distributed knowledge), readers reading readers (cascades), the stag hunt at the critical mass (02 §9, with Kandori-Mailath-Rob) and a code law (Lewis 1969, conventions). Cooperative AI (Dafoe et al. 2020) and multi-agent risk appear only in the alignment dossier and the reviews.
kept.what_is_missing: Nothing in the account states common knowledge or its role: Lewis 1969 on conventions, Aumann 1976 on agreement, Halpern and Moses 1990 (coordinated attack: coordination needs common knowledge, unattainable over unreliable channels), Rubinstein 1989 (the email game), Chwe 2001. Nor does it say whether pooling, which gives distributed knowledge, can give it. Aumann's theorem is recorded as a debt and not landed. Cooperative AI's framing is not joined to 05.
kept.why_it_matters: The stated purpose is that people and AI 'come to share an understanding and coordinate', and OPENING diagnoses a coordination failure with aligned incentives. That is the stag-hunt and common-knowledge problem, which the account models (stag hunt) without the epistemic half. A reader would take pooled coupling as the account's route to coordination, when the established result says distributed knowledge is not enough.
kept.suggested_work: State common knowledge on the grammar as the closure of the reach of the members' relations, the form the RF plan already sketches. Prove that pooled coupling (a meet) does not give it, with a witness. Join it to the critical-mass stag hunt: coordination on the payoff-dominant side needs common knowledge of the share. kept.title: The quantitative information-theoretic limits of control are absent; the selection and requisite-variety laws are their possibilistic shadow

kept.why_it_matters: This has the same shape as the proxy-problem case: a stronger quantitative result exists and is not brought in. The selection law is the account's 'centre' on the fronts. A graded form would make T3 and T6 more refutable: a drain bounded by unmeasured information, and early warning bounded by the mutual information with the need.
